summary: Sneak Point, an L-4 tower on the Clearwater National Forest, had a 1940 camp and was abandoned in 1941; the FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone. No source we read describes the site today.

events.note: Firelookout.com lists an L-4 tower in the 1930s, and the Forest Service list gives an L-4 tower of the same period.
A camp was set up on the eastern end of a spur that runs from the summit.
Abandoned 1941 in firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts.

evidence.supports: Clearwater County, on the Clearwater National Forest
About 6 miles east-southeast of Canyon Ranger Station
Camp atop the east end of a spur in 1940
evidence.quote: 1940: camp atop east end of spur off summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service list spells the name Sneak Peak. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts use Sneak Point, and the FFLA list does too, so the record keeps Sneak Point.

notes_for_editor: Location conflict is unresolved. The FFLA list gives 46.80395, -115.47140 (the value in our record). The Idaho Fire Lookouts record value, 46.80541, -115.49874, is about 2.1 km away, and the Idaho page text we read has no coordinates to check it against. Map check needed before any pin is published. Dates agree across firelookout.com, the Forest Service list and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The Forest Service list places it at Sec18 T40N R8E and gives elevation 4550 ft. No source describes the site today, and no removal date is given for the tower. No new photos added.
